title: Post-hoc task-LM output distributions and activation-cotangent diagnostics
status_note: Read-only evaluator and CPU observer tests prepared after initial RMS observations. No new task training, Dense teacher or GPU diagnostic result yet.

protocol.objective: Diagnose task-learning output/gradient behavior without optimizing Dense reconstruction
protocol.data: TRAIN prefix128 targets at each state; final four separate128-row calls at offsets0/4096/8192/12288 (512targets total), within qualified R<=256; no DEV/confirmation selection
measurements: input/output mean,std,RMS,max,exact/relative near-zero fractions,sampled absolute quantiles
input/output activation cotangent statistics at every block,norm,QKV,O,FFN up/down and residual FFN
raw parameter-gradient RMS and packed field RMS; do not compare coordinate magnitudes as identical parameterizations
centered covariance participation/stable rank on at most128 token rows; not full matrix rank
causal attention logit dispersion,entropy normalized by available keys,max probability,Q/K/V RMS
validation: preserve numerical Parameters and CPU/CUDA RNG
reproduce original128 TRAIN loss within1e-6 and FFN gradient RMS within atol1e-10/rtol1e-5
all underlying frozen training/audit/source controls remain unchanged
known-answer CPU uniform-attention and feature-rank tests; hooks preserve ordinary task gradients
hypotheses: initial attenuation versus learned signal-scale drift
realized update scale mismatch versus representation diversity/interaction
protocol.role_followup: Historical QKV success was width256/oldPolar and QKVO was width512/oldPolar. Matched current-recipe Q/K/V/O-only and combinations required before identifying O as the cause. This evaluator observes full-network behavior of the FFN cohorts; it is not that new attention-training study.
limitations: fixed TRAIN probes not the full data distribution
sample covariance rank bounded by token rows
same activation gradients comparable; parameter-coordinate gradients not directly comparable
